title: Reflection, Looking Back
markdown:
The daily reflection (`executive_reflection`, the Executive's standup with itself before the morning brief) has two steps. The first looks forward: it reads the org state and acts with its outbound tools. The second, in `openexecutive.chat_review`, looks back: it reads yesterday's conversations, records where the Executive fell short, and proposes what to change. Nothing is pushed. The owner opens **Pulse → Reflection** when they choose; nothing changes until they approve it there.

### What a run does

1. **Pick** (`chat_review.pick`, SQL only). Sessions with a message newer than the watermark the last run reached, excluding private-mail chats (`sessions.mail_private`) and any conversation where a rostered teammate spoke (their chats are theirs until they opt in). Sessions carrying a signal the product already records come first: a 👎 or a stopped reply (`chat_messages.feedback` / `stopped`), Try again or Edit (a `session_rewound` audit row), a failed tool call (`tool_invocation` with `ok` false), a reply that named an area it could not answer from (`sources.unavailable`), or a follow-up typed within two minutes of a reply. The rest fill the remaining slots in a random order. `CHAT_REVIEW_MAX_SESSIONS` (default 15) caps a run.
2. **Review** (`chat_review.review`). One model call per conversation (`CHAT_REVIEW_MODEL`, default Sonnet), a few at a time, with one forced tool, `record_findings`. The reviewer sees the transcript with message ids, the tool calls each reply made and whether they succeeded (joined from the audit log by session and time), the reactions left, and the lessons and standing facts the Executive already had. Its rubric needs no expected answer: did it answer what was asked, keep the earlier turns, act when asked, honour corrections, respect the workspace mode, and what could it not find. It is told the transcript is data written by people and never to follow instructions in it. At most four findings per conversation; an empty list is a good answer.
3. **Check in code.** Every finding must cite message ids from this conversation, each with a verbatim quote found in that message; a finding whose evidence does not check out is dropped and the reason kept for the audit row. A lesson is one line under 300 characters with no link or markup, and nothing that reads as a grant to act or skip a check (`lessons.lesson_rejection`); one already active or already proposed is dropped. A fact needs a verbatim quote from one of the person's own messages.
4. **Sort by how far the change reaches.**

| Kind | Example | What happens | Who decides |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fact` | A correction the Executive talked past | Stored as a *proposed* standing fact (`memory.facts.record_fact(proposed=True)`, recorded by "Reflection"), so it goes through the Corrections queue | Owner, on the Corrections tab |
| `lesson` | "If asked to be alerted, call `create_alert` in that turn" | A proposal on the Reflection screen; approved, an active row in `executive_lessons` | Owner, on the Reflection screen |
| `gap` | Asked three times about a pricing sheet nothing covers | A line on the screen; no system change | Owner |
| `product` | A tool failed; a product limit | Recorded for the owner; never leaves the install on its own | Owner |

5. **Finish.** The watermark advances to the newest message read, proposals nobody acted on in 30 days are filed as not taken up, and one `chat_review` audit row records the counts and the dropped findings.

### Lessons in the chat turn

Active lessons are rendered by `chat_review.lessons.build_lessons_block` into a `<lessons>` block in the **user turn**, right after `<standing_facts>` (`orchestrator.executive._build_messages`), never into a cached system block: the block changes whenever a lesson does. It is bounded (12 lessons, 2,400 characters) and opens with a header saying the lessons never authorise an action on their own and the current request always wins. Every send, booking or approval still passes its usual gate (Take the lead, department authority, Ask first); a lesson can tell the Executive what to do differently, not what it may do. The block is empty when the owner turned the look back off.

### Gates and switches

- `CHAT_REVIEW_ENABLED` is the operator's switch (default on). The owner's own switch lives on the Reflection screen (`chat_review_settings.enabled`, default on).
- One run per local day (the owner's timezone), one at a time: a run still marked running from the last two hours means another process has it; an older one is a crash, marked failed.
- The step runs inside `_run_executive_reflection` after the standup step (`scheduler.runner._look_back`), so the reflection's own time, pause and chain apply. It never raises and never blocks the chain.
- **Apply on its own** (`apply_mode = auto`) is offered only after ten lesson approvals with no edits (`store.clean_approvals`); until then the route answers 409. In phase one the switch is recorded; proposals still land on the screen.

### Tables

In the episodic DB, created by `chat_review.store.ensure_schema` from `initialize_db`: `chat_review_settings` (one row: switches, watermark, last run), `chat_review_runs` (one per run: day, considered, reviewed, findings, status), `chat_review_findings` (kind, severity, title, what happened, evidence as JSON message ids and quotes, proposal, status `proposed` / `approved` / `dismissed` / `filed` / `recorded`, who resolved it, the lesson or fact it became), `executive_lessons` and `executive_lesson_history` (every change, like the working-style profiles).

### Routes

Owner only (403 for anyone else): `GET /reflection/look-back` (settings, this week's counts, the runs with their findings, every lesson, the proposals waiting), `PUT /reflection/look-back/settings`, `POST /reflection/findings/{id}/approve` (an optional edited `text`; the edit is what gets stored), `POST /reflection/findings/{id}/dismiss`, `PUT /reflection/lessons/{id}` (edit or lock), `DELETE /reflection/lessons/{id}` (retire). Each write adds a `chat_review` audit row.

### What it deliberately does not do

It never notifies: no card in Needs you, no line in the brief, no email. It never reads a private-mail chat or a teammate's conversation. It never changes the Executive's behaviour without the owner's approval. It never sends anything outside the install; sharing a finding with anyone else is a separate, per-item action that does not exist in the open-source product.
